cards.text: Paul the apostle is writing a letter to Timothy, his true child in the faith (1 Timothy 1:1-2). Now Paul brings up a problem. What if anyone teaches another doctrine and disagrees with the sound words of our Lord Jesus Christ and with godly teaching?

cards.question: Paul says the person teaching against the sound words of Jesus really understands the truth and just explains it badly.

cards.text: Instead of the truth, Paul says this guy has an unhealthy interest in controversies and disputes about words. FORTY messages in the group chat, friend. All of them fighting over ONE word.

cards.question: Paul says something comes out of all those disputes about words. What is it?

answers.text: Envy and strife and evil suspicions

cards.text: On top of that comes constant friction between men of depraved mind who are devoid of the truth. And Paul says these men have their own idea of what godliness is for.

cards.question: Paul is describing men of depraved mind who are devoid of the truth. What do they think godliness is for?

cards.text: Here's the twist, friend. Paul says there IS great gain, and it comes from godliness paired with one other thing.

cards.question: Paul says godliness with ___ is great gain.

cards.text: Then Paul explains why. And he goes ALL the way back to the day you showed up in this world.

cards.question: Paul talks about coming into the world and leaving it. What does he say we bring in and carry out?

answers.text: Nothing in and a little out
A little in and nothing out

cards.text: Nothing in, nothing out. Me? I came out of a bakery bin with a 25-cent price sticker, and that sticker was my WHOLE estate. Then Paul names two things we will be content with.

cards.question: Paul says if we have ___ and ___ we will be content with these.

cards.text: Then Paul looks down the other road: people who want to be rich.

cards.question: Paul says those who want to be rich fall into ___.

cards.text: And they get ensnared by many foolish and harmful desires. Ensnared, friend, like me the day my mustache got caught in the dough mixer and I went around and AROUND and AROUND.

cards.question: Paul says the foolish and harmful desires of those who want to be rich plunge them into ruin and destruction.

cards.text: Then Paul digs all the way down to the root under all of it.

cards.question: Paul says money itself is the root of all kinds of evil.
Paul says some people craved money. What happened to them and the faith?
Paul says those who craved money ended up pierced with many sorrows. Who pierced them?

findings.problem: The heart of 6:10, that the love of money is the root of all kinds of evil, is only tested as a false statement ('money itself is the root'). No card ever states the true line. A baker who answers False learns what Paul didn't say, but never hears what he did say. Card 19 mentions craving money but never connects it to the root. Add a story card after card 18 that states it, or turn card 18 into a question whose right answer is 'the love of money'.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The card copies the BSB wording of 6:4–5 almost word for word ('constant friction between men of depraved mind who are devoid of the truth') with none of Papa Dorin's voice. It reads like a transcript, not a storyteller.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
